old: The players choose the summon together in step 3. Souls paid in step 1 are not returned, whichever card is chosen.
new: The players choose the summon together in step 3. If they cannot agree, the drawn data cards are shuffled face down and one is drawn. Souls paid in step 1 are not returned, whichever card is chosen.
rationale: Gives the one joint choice in the chapter that had no tie-break a tie-break that needs no token and no new term.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet picks the summon at random from the cards set aside (DS-Phantoms-Rules-lores.txt lines 238-240); Hollowed Edition: 'Summons are chosen at random' (line 389).

old: A summon has no *endurance bar* and pays no stamina. It has no *boss arcs* and no *heat-up* point, and its health is not scaled.
new: A summon has no *endurance bar* and pays no stamina. It has no *boss arcs* and no *heat-up* point, and its health is not scaled. A summon does only what its behaviour cards and its data card direct. It takes no *minor action* and no *major action*, and it cannot *parry*.
rationale: States in one place what a summon cannot do, so that no player asks whether a model with dodge dice may parry, walk, or attack outside its card.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet: summons are 'partially controlled by their behaviour cards and partially controlled by the players' and 'have fewer options each activation' (lines 236-239, 259-261); a data card shows block, resist and dodge only (lines 152-158).

old: Standard invaders appear before the *mini-boss* is defeated, and advanced invaders after it (see §2.4).
new: Standard invaders appear before the *mini-boss* is defeated, and advanced invaders after it (see §2.4). In campaign play, standard invaders appear while the current tier is tier one, and advanced invaders once it is tier two (see §18.5).
rationale: A campaign has several mini-bosses or none, so 'the mini-boss' names no moment there; the current tier is the one switch every campaign has, and it keeps the stronger invaders in step with the stronger treasure.
evidence: §18.5 and §18.7 of this book (tier two opens only when the bonfire ascetic is burnt); official Phantoms booklet ties the split to 'the mini boss' of a one-mini-boss game only (lines 363-377).

old: - During the exploration: when a character becomes embered by discarding an *ember card* (see §7.3), if one or more face-down encounter cards lie on the encounter tiles.
new: - During the exploration: when a character becomes embered by discarding an *ember card* (see §7.3), if one or more face-down encounter cards that carry no black cube lie on the encounter tiles (see §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
rationale: A reset turns every encounter card face down, cleared ones included; without the qualifier an invader token can land on an encounter the party skips and the invasion is wasted.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet: tokens go to 'each unexplored encounter tile' (lines 363-369); Hollowed Edition: 'place invader tokens on all undefeated encounters' (lines 342-343); §11.5 step 1 of this book.

old:
No more than one invasion is provoked before the mini-boss is defeated, and no more than one after it. Once an invasion has been provoked, no further invasion is provoked in that part of the game, however many characters are or become embered. If no character is embered when the encounter cards are dealt, no invader token is placed at that step.

The embering of every character at a boss's defeat (see §16.5) provokes no invasion at that moment. The invasion that follows the mini-boss's defeat is provoked when the encounter cards of the next setup are dealt (see §6.6).
new: No more than one invasion is provoked before the mini-boss is defeated, and no more than one after it, however many characters are or become embered. The embering of every character at a boss's defeat provokes no invasion at that moment (see §16.5). The invasion that follows the mini-boss's defeat is provoked when the encounter cards of the next setup are dealt (see §6.6). In campaign play, no more than one invasion is provoked in each *section* (see §18.1).
rationale: Two paragraphs become one without losing a rule: the dropped sentences restated the two trigger moments; the campaign limit of §18.1 is cited where the limit is stated.
evidence: Gate 1 OQ-28 (one invasion per leg); §18.1, Section Setup of this book.

old: 2. Add blank invader tokens, face down, until there is one token for each face-down encounter card on the encounter tiles. If the blank tokens run out, make up the number with invader tokens of the kind not drawn in step 1; such a token is treated as blank when it is revealed.
new: 2. Add blank invader tokens, face down, until there is one token for each face-down encounter card that carries no black cube. If the blank tokens run out, make up the number with invader tokens of the kind not drawn in step 1; such a token is treated as blank when it is revealed.
rationale: Same qualifier as the trigger: a cleared encounter receives no token. The substitution rule for a shortage of blank tokens is kept unchanged.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet lines 363-369 (unexplored tiles only) and components list, three blank tokens (line 103).

old: 4. Place one token face down on each face-down encounter card.
new: 4. Place one token face down on each of those encounter cards.
rationale: Keeps step 4 in line with step 2.
evidence: Follows phantom-E06.

old: An invader token stays face down on its encounter card until the characters fight that encounter. It stays in place when the encounters are *reset* (see §11.5) and when the party skips its encounter (see §7.5, Encounter Start). Invader tokens still on the tiles when the mini-boss is defeated are returned to the supply unrevealed (see §6.6).
new: An invader token stays face down on its encounter card until the characters fight that encounter, and it stays in place when the encounters are *reset* (see §11.5). Invader tokens still on the tiles when the mini-boss is defeated are returned to the supply unrevealed (see §6.6).
rationale: Once tokens go only to encounter cards without a black cube, no encounter that holds a token can be skipped, so the skip clause is dead text and is cut.
evidence: §7.5, Encounter Start of this book: only an encounter whose card carries a black cube may be skipped.

old: *Example.* The Herald discards an ember card while two face-down encounter cards lie on the tiles ahead, before the mini-boss is defeated.
new: *Example.* The Herald discards an ember card while two face-down encounter cards, neither of which carries a black cube, lie on the tiles ahead, before the mini-boss is defeated.
rationale: The example states the condition the rule now names; its numbers are unchanged.
evidence: Follows phantom-E04 and phantom-E06.

old: The invader's treasure card is awarded to the party at once (see §7.7). The players decide which character receives it. If they cannot agree, the card goes to the character who holds the aggro token at that moment.
new: The invader's treasure card is awarded to the party at once, and the players decide which character receives it as for any card awarded to the party (see §7.7).
rationale: One tie-break, stated once in §7.7 and worded to cover a card awarded during an encounter, replaces a local restatement that differed from it by one phrase.
evidence: Gate 1 OQ-29 (tie-break to the aggro holder everywhere); official Phantoms booklet: treasure card gained 'immediately' (lines 528-533).

old: An invader is an enemy model and counts towards clearing an encounter. While the invader is on the tile, the encounter is not *cleared*: it is cleared only when every enemy model, the invader included, has been killed, or when the invader has vanished and every other enemy model has been killed (see §7.5, Encounter Resolution).
new: An invader is an enemy model, and its encounter is not *cleared* while it is on the tile (see §7.5, Encounter Resolution). An invader leaves the tile only when it is killed or when it vanishes.
rationale: The ruling is confirmed; the paragraph says the same thing in half the words and lets the general rule of §7.5 do the work.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet: the invader 'will fight alongside the other enemies present' and leaves only if killed or if the party is defeated (lines 492-495, 527-533).

old: Whenever a treasure card is awarded to the party rather than to a named character (a chest's card, a mimic's cards, a boss treasure card, or the *mega-boss* treasure card of a Level 4 encounter), the players decide which character receives it. If they cannot agree, the card goes to the character who holds the aggro token when the encounter ends.
new: Whenever a treasure card is awarded to the party rather than to a named character (a chest's card, a mimic's cards, an invader's treasure card, a Titanite Scale card, a boss treasure card, or the *mega-boss* treasure card of a Level 4 encounter), the players decide which character receives it. If they cannot agree, the card goes to the character who holds the aggro token when the card is awarded.
rationale: The list now names every card awarded to the party, and 'when the card is awarded' covers a card gained during an encounter as well as one gained at its end.
evidence: Gate 1 OQ-29; §12.2, Invader Rewards and §14 of this book.

old: If crystal lizards are in play, a character who kills a crystal lizard takes one Titanite Scale card at once (see §14). A killed invader awards its treasure (see §12.2).
new: If crystal lizards are in play, a killed crystal lizard awards the party one Titanite Scale card at once (see §14). A killed invader awards its treasure card at once (see §12.2).
rationale: Keeps §7.7 in step with §14: the Titanite Scale card is awarded to the party, whatever killed the crystal lizard.
evidence: Official Iron Keep booklet: 'add one Titanite Scale card to the inventory', the party's shared inventory (DS-IronKeep-Rules-Web.txt lines 125-127).

old:
(see §13).
5. If *invaders* are in play, place the *invader tokens* on the encounter cards (see §12.2).
new:
(see §13).
5. If *invaders* are in play and any character is *embered*, place the *invader tokens* on the encounter cards (see §12.2).
rationale: The step read as unconditional although §12.2 places tokens at setup only when a character is embered.
evidence: §12.2, Invasions of this book; official Phantoms booklet places tokens only 'when a character gains an Ember token' (lines 363-366).

old: 15. If *invaders* are in play, place the *invader tokens* on the encounter cards (see §12.2).
new: 15. If *invaders* are in play and any character is *embered*, place the *invader tokens* on the encounter cards (see §12.2).
rationale: Same wording as §6.5 step 5, so that the two setups state the same condition.
evidence: §12.2, Invasions of this book.

old: When an *invasion* is provoked, one invader token is placed face down on each face-down encounter card, and each is revealed when the characters fight that encounter (see §12.2).
new: When an *invasion* is provoked, one invader token is placed face down on each face-down encounter card that carries no black cube, and each is revealed when the characters fight that encounter (see §12.2).
rationale: Keeps the component note in step with §12.2.
evidence: Follows phantom-E06.

old: A *summon* does not hold the aggro token, and damage inflicted by a summon does not move it (see §12.1).
new: A *summon* does not hold the aggro token, and damage inflicted by a summon does not move it. While the Distract icon of a summon's behaviour card is in effect, the boss treats the summon as the holder (see §12.1).
rationale: §16.4 owns boss aggro and did not mention the one effect that redirects it; the sentence points to §12.1 without restating the rule.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet, Distract (lines 293-298).

old: - Mimic: the chest is a mimic. A *mimic encounter* begins at once, before any recovery or reward (see §13.2).
new: - Mimic: the chest is a mimic. A *mimic encounter* begins at once, before the recovery and the rewards of the cleared encounter (see §13.2).
rationale: 'Before any recovery' no longer holds once the characters shed their stamina cubes before the mimic's first turn.
evidence: Follows phantom-E19.

old: The characters begin the mimic encounter as the cleared encounter left them. Each character keeps their damage cubes, stamina cubes, and condition tokens, and the *aggro token* stays with its holder.
new: Before the mimic's first turn, each character removes every stamina cube from their *endurance bar*. Nothing else is recovered. Each character keeps their damage cubes and condition tokens, no token is turned to its ready side, and the *aggro token* stays with its holder.
rationale: The ambush stays dangerous because damage carries over, but the fight no longer opens with characters who cannot act, and the party has no reason to stall on the last enemy to shed stamina before opening a chest.
evidence: Audit finding B-035 (approved at Gate 1, not applied: CH-13-022); official Explorers booklet removes all cubes before the mimic (DS-Explorers-Rules-Web.txt lines 464-467); Hollowed Edition: 'Players heal as normal' before opening (lines 378-380).

old: The Hungry Mimic is fought if the mini-boss has not been defeated, and the Voracious Mimic if it has.
new: The Hungry Mimic is fought if the mini-boss has not been defeated, and the Voracious Mimic if it has. In campaign play, the Hungry Mimic is fought while the current tier is tier one, and the Voracious Mimic once it is tier two (see §18.5).
rationale: Same anchor as for invaders: a campaign has no single mini-boss, and the mimic's extra card is drawn from the treasure deck of the current tier, so the stronger mimic guards the stronger treasure.
evidence: §13.3 step 2, §18.5 and §18.7 of this book; official Explorers booklet: 'a mini boss' (lines 476-482).

old: 4. Return the chest token and the *ambush card* to the supply.
new: 4. Return the chest token to its node, open side up, and the *ambush card* to the supply.
rationale: An opened chest already stays on its node for the rest of the game; treating the looted mimic's chest the same way removes an exception from §5.5, §7.5 and §11.5.
evidence: §5.5, Chests of this book ('an opened chest is never closed again'); official Explorers booklet removes only the mimic (lines 549-556).

old: A killed mimic does not return. Its chest token is not placed again when the encounter is *reset*, and the chest's node is used as a basic node (see §5.1).
new: A killed mimic does not return. Its chest stays on its node as an opened chest (see §5.5, Chests).
rationale: Follows the change to step 4: no special terrain state is left behind by a killed mimic.
evidence: §5.5, Chests of this book.

old: The Hungry Mimic replaces the chest token, takes the first turn, and attacks the Knight, who still carries all seven cubes. The characters kill the mimic. The party gains the chest's treasure card and one card drawn from the tier one treasure deck. Each character then gains four souls and one of the treasure cards dealt to the tile, and the Knight removes all four stamina cubes and one damage cube.
new: The Hungry Mimic replaces the chest token, and the Knight removes the four stamina cubes. The mimic takes the first turn and attacks the Knight, who still carries the three damage cubes. The characters kill the mimic. The party gains the chest's treasure card and one card drawn from the tier one treasure deck. Each character then gains four souls and one of the treasure cards dealt to the tile, and the Knight removes the stamina cubes placed during the mimic encounter and one damage cube.
rationale: The example now computes from §13.2 as amended: stamina cubes are removed before the mimic's first turn, damage cubes are kept.
evidence: Follows phantom-E19; Level 2 full reward of four souls from the table in §7.6.

old: When a character kills a crystal lizard, that character takes one Titanite Scale card from the supply at once and places it in their *inventory* (see §4.2).
new: When a crystal lizard is killed, the party is awarded one Titanite Scale card from the supply at once (see §4.2). The players decide which character receives it, as for any card awarded to the party (see §7.7).
rationale: An award to the party needs no rule for a crystal lizard killed by a condition or by an attack that hits several models, and it treats this card as every other card won from a kill is treated.
evidence: Official Iron Keep booklet: the card is added 'to the inventory', which is shared (lines 125-127); §7.7 of this book.

old: Once a crystal lizard has been killed in an encounter, no crystal lizard is placed in that encounter again, however many times the encounter is *reset* and fought (see §11.5). The party marks the tile to record the kill, for example by laying the killed model upside down beside the tile's encounter card. Until a crystal lizard has been killed there, the crystal lizards are placed again each time the encounter is set up.
new: Once a crystal lizard has been killed in an encounter, no crystal lizard is placed in that encounter again, however many times the encounter is *reset* and fought (see §11.5). To record the kill, one *damage cube* is placed on the encounter card of that encounter, where it stays until the card is returned to the game box. Until a crystal lizard has been killed there, the crystal lizards are placed again each time the encounter is set up.
rationale: A definite marker in the book's own idiom (a cube on the encounter card, as for a cleared encounter) replaces an example that fails on the second marked tile, because only two crystal lizard models are supplied.
evidence: §2.2 of this book (2x Crystal Lizard); official Iron Keep booklet suggests 'an opened chest token beside the tile' (lines 128-131); §7.5 (black cube marks a cleared encounter).

old: The icons and text of an attack option apply to a defender as they apply to an enemy (see §10.3).
new: The icons and text of an attack option apply to a defender as they apply to an enemy (see §10.3). In a PvP encounter, the word enemy in a *heroic action* or on a treasure card means another character.
rationale: The setup readies every heroic action token, so the chapter must say whether a heroic action that names an enemy works; one sentence extends the rule already stated for attack options.
evidence: §20.1 step 3 and §3.5, Heroic Action of this book; no official or community PvP rules exist to consult.

old: 4. Add one to the result for each *victory bonus* the attacker holds (see §20.8).
new: 4. Add one to the result if the attacker holds the *victory bonus* (see §20.8).
rationale: The victory bonus is no longer cumulative.
evidence: Source manuscript, chapter PLAYER VS PLAYER: 'Victory on non-final bosses provides +1 attack damage in future PvP only' (a flat +1; cumulation was added by CMP-0009).

old:
The dodge difficulty is given by the same table.
- The defender may decline to defend. The defender suffers damage equal to the attack value and is hit.
new: The dodge difficulty is given by the same table.
rationale: Blocking and resisting cost nothing and never leave the defender worse off than no defence, so the fourth option is never the right choice and only lengthens the list.
evidence: §9.4 of this book (a block or resist costs no stamina; with no dice the defence total is zero).

rationale: The six rows hold three values; three rows are easier to remember and change no result.
evidence: Audit B_report.md §10.1 (probabilities for the green die) and finding B-024.

old: When a character wins a PvP encounter that follows the defeat of a boss other than the final boss, the character gains one *victory bonus*. One *wound token* of value 1 is placed beside the winner's dashboard to mark it. In every subsequent PvP encounter, the character adds one to the *attack value* of each of their attacks for each victory bonus held (see §20.4). Victory bonuses are cumulative, have no effect outside PvP encounters, and are kept until the game ends.
new: When a character wins a PvP encounter that follows the defeat of a boss other than the final boss, the character gains the *victory bonus*. A spare token of any kind is placed beside the winner's dashboard to mark it. In every subsequent PvP encounter, the character adds one to the *attack value* of each of their attacks (see §20.4). A character holds no more than one victory bonus, however many PvP encounters the character wins. The victory bonus has no effect outside PvP encounters and is kept until the game ends.
rationale: A flat +1 gives the earlier contests a stake without deciding the last one in advance; a cumulative bonus reaches +4 or +5 in a campaign of five or six bosses. A spare token replaces the value 1 wound token, of which the core set has six and enemies need all.
evidence: Source manuscript PvP bullets (flat +1); §2.8 of this book (6x wound tokens of value 1); §19 (campaigns list up to six bosses).

old: *Example.* The Assassin wins the PvP encounter that follows the mini-boss, and one wound token is placed beside the Assassin's dashboard.
new: *Example.* The Assassin wins the PvP encounter that follows the mini-boss, and a spare token is placed beside the Assassin's dashboard.
rationale: Keeps the example in step with the marker named in the rule.
evidence: Follows phantom-E30.

old: It is the one rest that follows the boss's defeat (see §16.5); a PvP encounter grants no second rest.
new: It is the one rest that follows the boss's defeat (see §16.5); a PvP encounter grants no second rest. In campaign play, what follows a PvP encounter is stated with the campaign rules (see §18.1, Player versus Player Encounters).
rationale: §18.1 already settles PvP encounters in a campaign; §20.9 lacked the pointer.
evidence: §18.1, Player versus Player Encounters of this book.

old: **Invader token.** A token from the Phantoms expansion that shows an invader or is blank. When an *invasion* is provoked, one token is placed face down on each face-down encounter card, one of them showing an invader; a token is revealed when the characters fight that encounter (see §12.2).
new: **Invader token.** A token from the Phantoms expansion that shows an invader or is blank. When an *invasion* is provoked, one token is placed face down on each face-down encounter card that carries no black cube, one of them showing an invader; a token is revealed when the characters fight that encounter (see §12.2).
rationale: Keeps the entry in step with §12.2, Invader Tokens.
evidence: Follows phantom-E06.

old: **Invasion.** The placing of invader tokens that brings one invader into the game. An invasion is provoked when the encounter cards are dealt while a character is *embered*, or when a character becomes embered by discarding an *ember card* while a face-down encounter card lies on a tile; no more than one is provoked before the mini-boss is defeated and no more than one after it (see §12.2).
new: **Invasion.** The placing of invader tokens that brings one invader into the game. An invasion is provoked when the encounter cards are dealt while a character is *embered*, or when a character becomes embered by discarding an *ember card* while a face-down encounter card that carries no black cube lies on a tile; no more than one is provoked before the mini-boss is defeated and no more than one after it (see §12.2).
rationale: Keeps the entry in step with §12.2, Invasions.
evidence: Follows phantom-E04.

old: **Weak arc.** A boss arc shown in red on the arc diagram of the boss's current behaviour card, the card it drew most recently. A character who attacks a boss from a weak arc adds one black die to each attack roll, however many weak arcs the character is in (see §15.6).
new: **Weak arc.** A boss arc shown in red on the arc diagram of the boss's current behaviour card, the card it drew most recently. A character or a *summon* that attacks a boss from a weak arc adds one black die to each attack roll, however many weak arcs the attacker is in (see §15.6).
rationale: §12.1 and §15.6 give the weak-arc die to a summon; the entry named characters only.
evidence: Official Phantoms booklet: 'Summons, like characters, gain an additional black die on attacks in the weak arc' (lines 264-266).

old: **Turn.** One model's opportunity to act. In each round the enemies take their turns, then the characters take theirs in descending threat order (see §7.5, Encounter Turn Order; §10.1). In a boss encounter the boss takes a turn before each character's turn, and the players choose the order of the characters (see §16.1).
new: **Turn.** One model's opportunity to act. In each round the enemies take their turns, then the characters take theirs in descending threat order (see §7.5, Encounter Turn Order; §10.1). In a boss encounter the boss takes a turn before each character's turn, and the players choose the order of the characters (see §16.1). An *invader* takes a turn after each character's turn, and so does a *summon* in a boss encounter (see §12).
rationale: The entry omitted the two models whose turns follow each character's turn.
evidence: §12.1, Summon Turns and §12.2, Invader Turns of this book.

old: **Crystal lizard.** An optional enemy from the Iron Keep expansion, placed on a terrain node that the encounter card marks with the crystal lizard symbol. It flees rather than fights, is not scaled, does not count towards clearing the encounter, and escapes without award when the encounter is *cleared*. The character who kills one takes a Titanite Scale card, and once one has been killed in an encounter none is placed there again (see §14).
new: **Crystal lizard.** An optional enemy from the Iron Keep expansion, placed on a terrain node that the encounter card marks with the crystal lizard symbol. It flees rather than fights, is not scaled, does not count towards clearing the encounter, and escapes without award when the encounter is *cleared*. Killing one awards the party a Titanite Scale card, and once one has been killed in an encounter none is placed there again (see §14).
rationale: Keeps the entry in step with §14: the card is awarded to the party.
evidence: Follows phantom-E24.

old: **Mimic encounter.** The encounter fought against a *mimic* on the tile of a *cleared* encounter whose chest the party has opened. It is fought as a mini-boss encounter without arcs, with the characters on the nodes they occupy and before any recovery or reward (see §13.2).
new: **Mimic encounter.** The encounter fought against a *mimic* on the tile of a *cleared* encounter whose chest the party has opened. It is fought as a mini-boss encounter without arcs, with the characters on the nodes they occupy. The characters remove their stamina cubes before the mimic's first turn; the recovery and the rewards of the cleared encounter wait until the mimic is killed (see §13.2).
rationale: Keeps the entry in step with §13.2 as amended.
evidence: Follows phantom-E19.

old: **Victory bonus.** The reward for winning a *PvP encounter* that follows the defeat of a boss other than the final boss, marked by one wound token of value 1 placed beside the winner's dashboard. Each victory bonus adds one to the attack value of each of the character's attacks in every subsequent PvP encounter; victory bonuses are cumulative and are kept until the game ends (see §20.8).
new: **Victory bonus.** The reward for winning a *PvP encounter* that follows the defeat of a boss other than the final boss, marked by a spare token placed beside the winner's dashboard. It adds one to the attack value of each of the character's attacks in every subsequent PvP encounter. A character holds no more than one victory bonus, and it is kept until the game ends (see §20.8).
rationale: Keeps the entry in step with §20.8: one bonus, not cumulative, marked by a spare token.
evidence: Follows phantom-E30.

old: **A.** Not always. While the invader is on the tile, the encounter is not cleared. It is cleared when every enemy model, the invader included, has been killed, or when the invader has vanished and every other enemy model has been killed (see §12.2, End of an Invasion).
new: **A.** Yes, unless it vanishes. The encounter is not cleared while the invader is on the tile, and the invader leaves the tile only when it is killed or when the death of a character makes it vanish (see §12.2, End of an Invasion).
rationale: Same rule, answered the way the question is asked and in the words of §12.2 as amended.
evidence: Follows phantom-E11.

old: **A.** The mimic encounter is failed, and with it the encounter that held the chest. The mimic returns to its chest, and the characters must rest at the bonfire. Each later time that encounter is cleared, the party again decides whether to open the chest (see §13.4).
new:
**A.** The mimic encounter is failed, and with it the encounter that held the chest. The mimic returns to its chest, and the characters must rest at the bonfire. Each later time that encounter is cleared, the party again decides whether to open the chest (see §13.4).

**Q.** Do the characters recover before a mimic is fought?

**A.** They remove their stamina cubes and nothing else. Each character keeps their damage cubes and condition tokens, and a character who died in the cleared encounter stays dead. The recovery and the rewards of the cleared encounter follow the mimic's death (see §13.2; §13.3).
rationale: Players who know the published rule expect a full recovery before the mimic; the answer states this book's rule as amended.
evidence: Follows phantom-E19.
